audit_notes: Parameters are plausible. Checks: (1) Re_L = 7.7*200/1.19e-6 = 1.3e9, CF0 (ITTC-57) = 0.075/(log10 Re - 2)^2 = 1.48e-3, tau_w = 0.5*1025*7.7^2*1.48e-3 = 45 Pa, u_tau = 0.21 m/s, viscous length 5.7 um. (2) Townsin added friction: AHR 125 um gives 1000*dCF = 44*((6.25e-7)^(1/3) - 10*Re^(-1/3)) + 0.125 = 0.096, i.e. +6.5 % of CF0; AHR 40 um gives about 0. The formulator's negative-slip closure (roughness_offset_coefficient 0.141 times AHR above a 35 um smooth threshold) is calibrated to this correlation, so the model reproduces Townsin rather than predicting it independently; its value is the transparent parameter dependence on AHR. (3) Glass-flake vinyl-ester coats reach AHR 40-60 um as applied and keep it for 10+ years under regular grooming; flake 3 um x 50 um gives a nacre-like aspect ratio of about 17 for toughness. (4) Structural: hard coat, abrasion-resistant, no structural concern; impact cracking at very low temperature is a minor risk. (5) Not captured: fouling between grooming intervals; without grooming the hard coat fouls like any inert surface and loses far more than 6 %. Baseline: conventional new paint system at AHR 125 um (coating_hull_roughness = 1.25e-4; this is outside the coating's own design bound but is the reference paint, not a design value).
